Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We combine classical methods of combinatorial group theory with the theory of small cancellations over relatively hyperbolic groups to construct finitely generated torsion-free groups that have only finitely many classes of conjugate elements. Moreover, we present several results concerning embeddings into such groups.   As another application of these techniques, we prove that every countable group $C$ can be realized as a group of outer automorphisms of a group $N$, where $N$ is a finitely generated group having Kazhdan's property (T) and containing exactly two conjugacy classes.

The authors combine methods from combinatorial group theory with techniques from small cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups. This combination allows them to construct and analyze groups with highly unusual conjugacy properties while still maintaining strong control over their algebraic structure.

One of their main achievements is the construction of finitely generated torsion-free groups that have only finitely many conjugacy classes. Such groups are striking because, in most familiar infinite groups, conjugacy classes are abundant and reflect a rich internal structure. Producing torsion-free examples with only finitely many conjugacy classes therefore requires delicate methods, particularly to ensure that the groups remain finitely generated and do not acquire unwanted torsion.

The authors also establish several embedding results concerning groups with finitely many conjugacy classes. These results show that a wide range of groups can be embedded into larger groups whose conjugacy structure is extremely restricted. In this way, the paper demonstrates that having finitely many conjugacy classes is compatible with containing many different kinds of subgroups, revealing a surprising flexibility in this class of groups.

Another major result is that every countable group can be realized as the outer automorphism group of some group. In other words, given any countable group \(Q\), the authors construct a group \(G\) such that
\[
\operatorname{Out}(G) \cong Q.
\]
This provides a very general realization theorem for outer automorphism groups and shows that outer automorphism groups can be as complicated as arbitrary countable groups.

Finally, the authors construct a group \(N\) with particularly strong properties. The group \(N\) is finitely generated, torsion-free, and has Kazhdan’s property (T), a rigidity property with important consequences in representation theory and geometric group theory. Remarkably, \(N\) contains exactly two conjugacy classes. Thus all nontrivial elements of \(N\) are conjugate to one another, while the identity element forms the other conjugacy class. This construction illustrates the power of the authors’ methods and provides an especially dramatic example of a group with an extremely small number of conjugacy classes.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a research article proving the existence of finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes and realizing any countable group as Out(N) for a property (T) group N with two conjugacy classes.
counterfactuals.output:
The article’s main achievements are two striking existence results in combinatorial/geometric group theory.

### 1. Finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes

The authors prove that there exist infinite finitely generated torsion-free groups with only finitely many conjugacy classes. In the torsion-free case, the strongest possible nontrivial version is obtained: a group with exactly two conjugacy classes,

\[
\{1\} \quad \text{and} \quad G\setminus \{1\}.
\]

Thus every nonidentity element is conjugate to every other nonidentity element.

This is remarkable because finitely generated infinite groups usually have infinitely many conjugacy classes, and having only two conjugacy classes forces very rigid algebraic behavior. For example, such a group is necessarily simple: any nontrivial normal subgroup contains one nonidentity element, hence contains all nonidentity elements.

The construction uses small-cancellation techniques over relatively hyperbolic groups, allowing one to impose conjugacy relations while preserving torsion-freeness and finite generation.

---

### 2. Realizing arbitrary countable groups as outer automorphism groups

The article also proves that for every countable group \(Q\), there exists a finitely generated group \(N\) such that

\[
\operatorname{Out}(N) \cong Q,
\]

where \(N\) has Kazhdan’s property \((T)\) and exactly two conjugacy classes.

So \(N\) is highly rigid from the viewpoint of representation theory/property \((T)\), extremely homogeneous from the viewpoint of conjugacy, yet its outer automorphism group can be prescribed arbitrarily among countable groups.

In particular, the result shows that even within the very restrictive class of finitely generated property \((T)\) groups with only two conjugacy classes, the possible outer automorphism groups are as flexible as possible: every countable group occurs.

---

### Conceptual significance

The paper combines two themes that might seem incompatible:

- **Extreme internal rigidity:** property \((T)\), torsion-freeness, simplicity, and only two conjugacy classes.
- **Extreme external flexibility:** arbitrary countable groups can appear as \(\operatorname{Out}(N)\).

The main technical engine is a refined small-cancellation construction over relatively hyperbolic groups, designed to simultaneously force prescribed conjugacy behavior and control automorphisms. The results extend earlier work on groups with few conjugacy classes and on realizing groups as outer automorphism groups, showing that these phenomena persist even under strong finiteness and rigidity constraints.

**Abstract.**  
We construct new examples of finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes, including groups in which all nontrivial elements are conjugate. The construction is based on small-cancellation methods over relatively hyperbolic groups and allows substantial control over both conjugacy and automorphism structure. As an application, we prove that every countable group occurs as the outer automorphism group of a finitely generated group with Kazhdan’s property \((T)\) and exactly two conjugacy classes. Thus, despite the extreme restriction on conjugacy structure, finitely generated property \((T)\) groups can realize arbitrary countable groups as their outer automorphism groups. These results provide new evidence for the flexibility of pathological conjugacy behavior within finitely generated and rigidity-type group classes.

counterfactuals.output:
## Summary

This work develops a small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups and uses it to solve classical embedding and conjugacy-class problems in combinatorial group theory. The central theme is that the flexibility of classical small cancellation—traditionally used over free or hyperbolic groups—extends to the relative setting strongly enough to produce highly pathological but finitely generated torsion-free groups, including infinite groups with only finitely many conjugacy classes.

The paper combines two traditions:

1. **Classical combinatorial group theory**, especially the Higman–Neumann–Neumann philosophy of embedding countable groups into finitely generated groups with controlled conjugacy behavior.
2. **Modern relatively hyperbolic small cancellation**, allowing one to impose infinitely many relations on a relatively hyperbolic group while preserving key structural features such as torsion-freeness, infinitude, and relative hyperbolicity of the quotient.

A principal outcome is the construction of finitely generated torsion-free groups in which the number of conjugacy classes is finite—indeed, in strong forms, one can arrange that all nontrivial elements lie in a single conjugacy class. These examples are infinite, finitely generated, torsion-free, and far from residually finite; in particular, they have no nontrivial finite quotients.

---

## Main Ideas and Results

### 1. Small cancellation over relatively hyperbolic groups

The paper establishes a general small-cancellation machinery for groups that are hyperbolic relative to a collection of subgroups. Instead of working with ordinary van Kampen diagrams over free groups, one works with **relative presentations** and diagrams whose geometry reflects the peripheral structure.

The key technical theorem may be summarized as follows:

> Let \(G\) be a group hyperbolic relative to a family of subgroups. Under suitable relative small-cancellation hypotheses, quotienting \(G\) by a carefully chosen normal subgroup preserves relative hyperbolicity and controls torsion and embeddings of peripheral subgroups.

In particular, if \(G\) is torsion-free and the imposed relations are chosen appropriately, then the quotient remains torsion-free. Moreover, one can force specified elements to become conjugate in the quotient while retaining enough hyperbolic structure to continue the process inductively.

This is the technical engine behind the later embedding and conjugacy-class constructions.

---

### 2. Forcing conjugacy without collapsing the group

A major application is the ability to take a non-elementary relatively hyperbolic group \(G\) and impose relations that make chosen elements conjugate, while ensuring that the resulting quotient remains infinite and torsion-free.

Roughly, given nontrivial elements \(a,b \in G\), one adds relations of the form

\[
x^{-1} a x = b
\]

or more elaborate small-cancellation relations that force \(a\) and \(b\) to become conjugate in a quotient. The difficulty is to do this repeatedly—possibly infinitely many times—without destroying the group.

The relative small-cancellation theory guarantees that, if the conjugating words are chosen long and sufficiently independent, then the quotient does not degenerate. This allows an inductive construction in which more and more pairs of elements are identified up to conjugacy.

---

### 3. Finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes

Using the above machinery, the paper constructs finitely generated torsion-free groups with very few conjugacy classes.

A typical theorem is:

> There exists an infinite finitely generated torsion-free group with exactly two conjugacy classes: the identity class and the class of all nontrivial elements.

Equivalently, every two nontrivial elements are conjugate.

More generally, one can build torsion-free finitely generated groups with a prescribed finite number of conjugacy classes, subject to the obvious restrictions imposed by torsion.

These examples are striking because finitely generated groups usually have infinitely many conjugacy classes. In residually finite groups, for instance, finite quotients often separate conjugacy classes, making such behavior impossible. Thus the constructed groups are necessarily highly non-residually finite.

---

### 4. Embedding theorems

The paper also proves strong embedding results in the spirit of Higman–Neumann–Neumann.

One form of the result is:

> Every countable torsion-free group embeds into a finitely generated torsion-free group with finitely many conjugacy classes.

In stronger versions, the ambient group can be arranged so that all nontrivial elements outside the embedded structure fall into prescribed conjugacy classes, or even so that all nontrivial elements of the ambient group are conjugate.

The construction begins by embedding the countable group into a suitable relatively hyperbolic group—often a free product or an HNN-type construction—and then applies the relative small-cancellation quotienting process to collapse conjugacy classes while preserving the embedded subgroup.

This gives a powerful refinement of classical embedding theory: not only can countable groups be embedded into finitely generated groups, but the ambient group can be made to have extremely restricted conjugacy structure.

---

### 5. Quotients of hyperbolic and relatively hyperbolic groups

Another important feature is that the groups constructed can often be obtained as quotients of well-behaved hyperbolic or relatively hyperbolic groups.

For example:

> Every non-elementary torsion-free hyperbolic group has an infinite torsion-free quotient in which all nontrivial elements are conjugate.

This is especially useful because many desirable properties pass to quotients. The construction can therefore be combined with known examples of hyperbolic groups having additional rigidity properties.

---

## Application to Kazhdan Property \((T)\)

A notable application concerns Kazhdan’s property \((T)\).

Property \((T)\) passes to quotients. Therefore, starting from a non-elementary torsion-free hyperbolic group with property \((T)\), the small-cancellation quotient construction produces an infinite finitely generated torsion-free group with property \((T)\) and finitely many conjugacy classes.

In particular, one obtains:

> There exists an infinite finitely generated torsion-free group with Kazhdan property \((T)\) and exactly two conjugacy classes.

This is a striking example. Such a group is simultaneously:

- infinite;
- finitely generated;
- torsion-free;
- Kazhdan;
- non-residually finite;
- without nontrivial finite quotients;
- and with all nontrivial elements conjugate.

The result illustrates the strength of relative small cancellation: it can impose extreme conjugacy constraints while preserving robust large-scale or representation-theoretic properties inherited from the original group.

---

## Conceptual Significance

The work shows that relative hyperbolicity provides a natural setting in which classical small-cancellation methods can be revived and substantially generalized. The resulting theory is flexible enough to control conjugacy, embeddings, torsion, and quotient structure simultaneously.

The main conceptual achievements are:

1. **A robust small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups.**
2. **Construction of finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes.**
3. **Embedding of countable torsion-free groups into finitely generated groups with prescribed conjugacy behavior.**
4. **Production of exotic quotients of hyperbolic groups.**
5. **Application to property \((T)\), yielding Kazhdan groups with extremely small conjugacy structure.**

Overall, the paper bridges classical combinatorial group theory and modern geometric group theory, showing that relative hyperbolicity is a powerful framework for constructing finitely generated groups with highly controlled—and highly unusual—algebraic behavior.
